test_title: PYST 27: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Ohm’s Law is valid under which condition?

options.text: For all materials at any temperature
Only for insulator at high temperatures
Only for metallic conductors at constant temperature

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only for metallic conductors at constant temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm’s Law** states that the **electric current** flowing through a **conductor** is directly proportional to the **potential difference** (voltage) applied across its ends, provided physical conditions like **temperature** and **pressure** remain constant.
 
• The mathematical expression for this law is **V = IR**, where **V** is the **Voltage**, **I** is the **Current**, and **R** is the **Resistance**.
 
• The law is primarily applicable to **metallic conductors** (such as **copper**, **silver**, and **aluminum**) because they exhibit a linear relationship between voltage and current. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***
 
• It is not valid for all materials at any temperature because as the **temperature** changes, the **resistance** of the material also changes, breaking the proportionality. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• **Semiconductors** (like **Silicon** and **Germanium**) do not follow Ohm’s law as they are **non-ohmic** devices where the **V-I characteristic** is non-linear. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• **Insulators** do not conduct electricity under normal conditions and do not follow this linear proportionality, even at high temperatures where their properties might break down. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin of the Law:** The law was named after the **German physicist Georg Simon Ohm**, who published his findings in his **1827** treatise, "The Galvanic Circuit Investigated Mathematically."
 
• **Resistance (R):** It is the property of a material to oppose the flow of current. The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm**, denoted by the Greek symbol **Ω**. One ohm is defined as the resistance of a conductor such that a **potential difference** of **1 Volt** causes a **current** of **1 Ampere** to flow.
 
• **Ohmic vs. Non-Ohmic Conductors:**
 
 
• **Ohmic Conductors:** Materials that obey Ohm's law, showing a straight-line **V-I graph** passing through the origin (e.g., **metals** at low/constant temperatures).
 
• **Non-Ohmic Conductors:** Materials that do not obey the law. Examples include **p-n junction diodes**, **transistors**, **vacuum tubes**, **thermistor**, and **electrolytes**. In these cases, the resistance is not constant and varies with the applied voltage or current.
 
 
 
• **Applications:** Ohm's law is fundamental in designing **electrical circuits**, determining the required **resistors** for **electronic devices**, and calculating **power consumption** (P = VI or P = I²R).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Temperature Sensitivity:** For **metallic conductors**, resistance increases with an **increase in temperature** because the **thermal agitation** of atoms increases, leading to more frequent collisions with **drift electrons**. The relation is given by **R = R₀[1 + α(T - T₀)]**, where **α** is the **temperature coefficient of resistance**.
 
• **Limitations:** Ohm’s law is not a fundamental law of nature like **Newton's laws**; rather, it is an empirical description of the behavior of certain materials. It fails under **high electric fields**, very **low temperatures** (superconductivity), or for **unilateral networks** (where current flows in only one direction, like **diodes**).
 
• **Drift Velocity:** The current in a conductor is related to the **drift velocity** of electrons. Under constant physical conditions, the drift velocity is proportional to the **electric field**, which underpins the validity of Ohm's Law.
